paper.title: DoReMi: Grounding Language Model by Detecting and Recovering from Plan-Execution Misalignment
paper.central_claim: LLM-generated skill plans and execution constraints, continuously checked by a VLM with immediate violation-triggered replanning, improve task success and execution time under disturbances on arm and humanoid tasks.

evidence.quote: Our contributions can be summarized as follows: • Different from previous works that use LLM only to plan, we leverage LLM to play a dual role, aiding not only in high-level planning but also generating constraints to supervise low-level execution. • We propose DoReMi, an integrated framework between LLMs and VLMs to enable more precise and frequent feedback automatically. • Experiments on robot arm manipulation tasks and humanoid robot tasks demonstrate that DoReMi leads to a higher task success rate and short
evidence.support_explanation: Author system-level SR/time claim; detector finetuning is one component, not the central claim type.

evidence.quote: During the low-level skill execution stage, we employ a vision-language model (VLM) [ 10 ] as a general ”constraint detector” that periodically verifies the satisfaction of all constraints. If any constraint is violated, the language model is invoked for immediate re-planning to facilitate recovery. III-A
evidence.support_explanation: Periodic constraint violation checks trigger immediate replanning, not end-of-skill retry alone.
